title: PCB Defense: Breach — bullet-heaven tower defense on a living PCB (AI-assisted key art and code, procedural in-game art)
author: MasterSteak4510
selftext:
I'm the developer. PCB Defense: Breach is a bullet-heaven tower defense on a

living circuit board, built in Godot 4.



How AI was used — the honest split:

\- In-game visuals: no AI-generated frames. The PCB traces, silkscreen, vias,

  pads, bugs and bosses are drawn procedurally in Godot. The board shader is

  one material, not a tile atlas.

\- Store/key art: AI-assisted (cover, banner, a few promo frames), disclosed on

  the itch page.

\- Code: AI-assisted pair programming for boilerplate and refactors; every

  gameplay system is human-reviewed and tested.



What is interesting technically: 800 bug bodies are one MultiMeshInstance2D.

No per-bug Node2D, no physics engine — positions and flags live in packed

arrays (\`PackedVector2Array\`, \`PackedByteArray\`, \`PackedFloat32Array\`) and one

linear pass per frame handles contact, stun and respawn. The boss body drops

detail tiers as the live horde grows, which took the demo Hydra from 617.9 to

442.4 average draw calls at 600 bodies on an M2.



Free browser demo (600-body preset, Compatibility renderer):

[https://juba13.itch.io/pcb-defense-breach](https://juba13.itch.io/pcb-defense-breach)



I'm happy to go deeper on the procedural board or the boss LOD.
